reason: Wording: checked against the text and not against a quotation site. The MediaWiki wikitext of the Wikisource transcription of Woman Rights Tracts No. 4, the reprint of the Westminster and Foreign Quarterly Review for July 1851, prints the sentence letter for letter as proposed, semicolon included: What is wanted for women is equal rights, equal admission to all social privileges; not a position apart, a sort of sentimental priesthood. Nothing is trimmed and no letter is raised. The Worcester Women History Project transcription agrees, and the two witnesses are independent of each other. Locator: the ordinal looked like the weak point and it holds. A first reading of the page suggested two paragraphs follow, which would have made this third from the close, but the raw source shows only one paragraph after it, the one beginning There are indications that the example of America will be followed on this side of the Atlantic, which closes the essay with the Sheffield petition presented to the House of Lords on 13 February 1851. So the sentence stands in the second paragraph from the close, exactly as the source line says, and that paragraph is about the Worcester convention resolutions: it objects to the fourth head of demand, the social and spiritual union verbiage, and the quoted sentence is the correction to it. Attribution: the essay appeared unsigned and was long taken for John Stuart Mill, which is the one real trap here, but Mill assigned it to his wife when he reprinted it, and both transcriptions head it with her name, so Harriet Taylor Mill is right. Not a character line, so no speaker to name. Scope: a review essay of 1851, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory, and it needs no warning. Tag Essay is the form of the work. Cap and shipped: shipped.js returns nothing shipped, no near opening, harriet taylor mill at 0 of 3, not banned. Source line: 128 characters, leads with the name, no dash. Theme: equal rights rather than a position apart is precisely what September means by what is owed, and it is bracing rather than bleak at six in the morning. One soft point that is not a refutation: the locator is descriptive rather than a page, and the tract prints the passage at pages 22 to 23 if the editor wants a harder one.
